open_issues: The shell's organisation band is a slot, not content: MPhoneScreen now has an `orgHeader` slot between the status strip and the bar, but WakeelShell leaves it empty because the organisation and office names only exist after pairing (M01-M04, a later package). The first screen package must fill that slot or the frame will differ from M06 onwards.

MBottomNav badges are not fed in the shell (no data source yet); the design previews show 3/5/12 on the nav items. The kit supports them and the gallery renders them, so this is purely a later-package wiring task.

Bouncy Castle (bcprov-jdk18on 1.78.1) had to be added to the catalog beyond the libraries the package names: Ed25519 and X25519 are not reachable through the platform providers at minSdk 29, and the .NET side's signatures and agreements must match exactly.

No instrumented (device) test runs: the package forbids starting an emulator, so SQLCipher on a real Android process and the Storage Access Framework WakeelFolder implementation are exercised only through their interfaces on the JVM (in-memory Room + java.io.File). They need an on-device pass in a later package.

The .NET AndroidVectorTests writes the vectors but nothing yet reads android/core/build/vectors-out/ back on the .NET side; that reverse test belongs to whichever package owns the Windows sync side (B7-1).

DESIGN DECISIONS — the frame is one composable, MPhoneScreen (status strip, organisation band slot, bar, padded scrolling content, bottom bar, floating action button, optional scrim overlay); a screen only fills the content slot with kit composables. RTL is the whole app's direction, set once in WakeelTheme, so every alignment is written as start/end and mirrors correctly. Bidi.wrap puts Unicode isolates around every string that can mix Arabic with Latin or digits, and every M.* composable wraps its own text, so a screen cannot forget it. Digits are Western everywhere, including the badge overflow "+99" (the old «+٩٩» comment in MFoundation.kt is gone). The container, canonical JSON and domain-separation code was written against src/Wakeel.Crypto rather than from the prose, and the byte-for-byte proof is the vector files the .NET test writes. The sync engine treats a file as whole only when its container verifies, so an interrupted write is simply invisible and gets rewritten; a packet is applied inside one Room transaction, and the receipt is written after the transaction commits, never before.
